doc.title: Dave McKenna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Eddie Condon as a character and guitarist
summary: McKenna remembers Condon as subdued but funny, a good rhythm guitarist who rarely took solos.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Was Eddie Condon as much of a character—

He was sort of subdued, but he was still a funny man. And he played. Oh he came up to play a few times. Usually he’d sit and talk with the people. But he played good rhythm and all the right chords. I hear he only took one solo in his life on a record, and it was a record with Fats Waller. Somebody told me that, I don’t know if that’s true.
Did he just play a four string guitar or something?
Wasn’t it a five string? I don’t know.
I’m not an expert on the guitar. I know who I like though. We’ve got a couple of good ones here.
